Photograph: Josh Reynolds/AP Massachusetts Judge denies defense motion to declare Lindsay Clancy not guilty of murder Request for Clancy, 36, to be acquitted turned down nearly a month after first trial ended with deadlocked jury Associated Press Thu 1 Oct 2026 16.27 EDT Last modified on Thu 1 Oct 2026 16.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case on Thursday refused to declare her not guilty, turning down a defense motion that had argued there was not enough evidence to prove she was responsible for killing her three children. On Tuesday, Clancy’s attorney Kevin Reddington tried to persuade Judge William Sullivan that prosecutors had not offered any proof that Clancy had killed her three children. Prosecutors argued there was plenty of evidence, calling Reddington’s claim “laughable”. In his ruling, Sullivan said prosecutors had provided adequate evidence for a jury to decide whether Clancy was the person responsible for the killings. “There was evidence introduced, both physical and circumstantial, that would permit a rational trier of fact to find beyond a reasonable doubt the elements of the charge of murder,” Sullivan wrote. During that trial, Reddington did not dispute that Clancy killed the children at the family’s home in 2023. Instead, the defense sought to persuade the jury that the 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse was not criminally responsible because of mental disease, a rare condition called postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors acknowledged that Clancy, 36, had mental health problems that included months of treatment and a stay in a psychiatric hospital, but argued that she knew what she was doing when she strangled the children then tried to kill herself. Clancy’s first trial ended with a deadlocked jury. A judge declared a mistrial with the jury split 11-1 in favor of acquitting Clancy of murder charges. The meeting followed Ukraine’s adoption of a minority education law and Hungary’s decision to stop blocking two areas of EU accession negotiations. New cooperation will focus on trade, border infrastructure, business contacts and people-to-people ties, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said, noting that Ukraine aims to open its remaining two accession clusters by year-end. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 16, 2026, 6:17 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar during an interview with the Austrian news agency APA in Vienna, Austria, on May 21, 2026. (Photo by ROLAND SCHLAGER / APA / AFP) / Austria OUT Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip President Volodymyr Zelensky and Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar agreed to normalize relations in Brussels on Friday, Oct. 16, ending months of tensions that have stalled Ukraine’s EU bid, bolstering Kyiv’s goal of opening all remaining accession clusters by year-end. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry described the meeting as historic, saying it marked an important step toward restoring ties between Kyiv and Budapest after years of friction over the rights of Ukraine’s Hungarian minority. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “Today, we have truly opened a new chapter. This is a reset across all tracks: political, economic, humanitarian and others,” Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said. The leaders met on the sidelines of the European Council summit after a breakthrough over minority education rights helped unblock part of Ukraine’s EU accession negotiations. Advertisement Trade, borders and business ties According to the ministry, bilateral cooperation will focus on trade and economic ties, border infrastructure, business contacts and people-to-people engagement. After the leaders’ talks, Sybiha met his Hungarian counterpart, Anita Orbán, to coordinate the implementation of the agreements. “This is how quiet and effective diplomacy works – in the interest of the nation, not headlines,” Sybiha said. Magyar, for his part, expressed solidarity with Ukraine against Russia’s aggression and offered diplomatic support for efforts to secure a ceasefire and lasting peace, Reuters reported , citing his Facebook statement after the meeting. Other Topics of Interest ‘Not Trump’s Decision’: Lukashenko Says Ukrainians Must Choose Their President Belarusian leader rejected Trump’s attempt to dictate Ukraine’s leadership but also argued that Zelensky should face an election. The reset comes ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution against Soviet rule. Minority education law helps unblock EU talks Ukraine’s parliament adopted the education amendments on Oct. 12, and Zelensky signed them into law that day. The legislation expands education rights for national minorities whose languages are official EU languages and introduces a special status for qualifying minority-language schools. Advertisement The rights of Ukraine’s ethnic Hungarian community, concentrated in the southwestern Zakarpattia region, have long been a source of tension with Budapest. Both Magyar’s government and its predecessor, led by Viktor Orbán, linked progress in Ukraine’s accession negotiations to minority-rights concerns. After the law’s adoption, Hungary dropped its objections to opening Cluster 2, covering the internal market, and Cluster 3, covering competitiveness and inclusive growth. Negotiations on both opened on Oct. 13 , bringing the total opened to four of the six clusters. So far, Ukraine and Moldova opened Cluster 1 – Fundamentals on June 15, and Cluster 6 – External Relations on July 14. Ukraine aims to open Cluster 4, on the green agenda and sustainable connectivity, and Cluster 5, on resources, agriculture and cohesion – before the end of 2026. Magyar described the law and the start of its implementation as a step toward restoring mutual trust. He said discussions would continue at ministerial level. The move comes just a day after the EU officials removed ‘urgency’ language from their draft summit conclusions on opening Ukraine’s and Moldova’s remaining negotiating clusters on Oct. 15, softening the timeline on the accession. Advertisement The updated draft keeps the expectation that the clusters will be opened under the merit-based approach but no longer includes any reference to timing. Fu rther meeting s under consideration Further talks could take place in Berehove , a center of Ukraine’s Hungarian community, Magyar said, according to Euronews. Zelensky has also received an invitation to Budapest for the Oct. 23 commemoration of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution, deputy presidential chief of staff Ihor Zhovkva told Euronews. He said the president was considering attending; a visit has not been confirmed. The Brussels summit comes as Zelensky seeks European support amid continuing Russian attacks and tensions with Washington over restrictions on military satellite communications and US policy toward Russian energy exports .
